parsed.explanation: The dossier shows no trans-specific criminal offence, no documented border/facility/custody exclusion, and no pattern of police targeting or anti-trans violence; same-sex conduct is not criminalised. But it is thin and dated, with no documented social acceptance of trans identity and no functioning anti-discrimination recourse. The state tolerates LGBTI people only conditionally—unless they campaign or are judged publicly immodest/indecent—and blocks LGBTI webpages, while media discussion is rare and trans people appear mainly as entertainment. Societal discrimination is reported, though LGB-wide and from 2013. A trans visitor who is outed therefore faces moderate social and possible official friction with little remedy, but no evidence of severe penalties or organised targeting. Open questions on facilities, detention, and care are not counted as proven exposures.
